title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday, 20% of the week. No prior closure data, but impact is direct and measurable. Recent weeks show no adjustment for partial closures.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 7.6 is adjusted downward due to the store closure on Monday (1/5 of the week), reducing demand by ~20%. The price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) is not expected to drive uplift given past price tests showed no lift (x1.03, x1.11). The classical uplift model's x1.00 is appropriate—no promotion or event is active. The back-to-school season has passed; recent weeks show no trend. The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is minimal (x1.16), and no post-promotion dip is observed. The closure is a clear, named driver with direct impact. Evidence is strong but single-occurrence for the closure.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 35.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 23.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
